investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict) — production-api
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T22:35:40–44Z with an identical 409 response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected the creation request because the agent quota for the eval org has reached its hard limit of 100. Because the agent creation call fails immediately, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is ever written, causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner. The eval org used by the status probes has accumulated 100 swarm agents — the enforced per-org limit — leaving no capacity for the eval to create a new remote agent. Because agent creation is the first step in the runner branch (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339: `const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)`), all downstream evidence collection and contract assertions are skipped, producing a complete evidence gap and a fail status across all three remote-agents checks.

Less likely but possible: the eval runner's withCleanup mechanism is functioning but a prior run crashed before cleanup executed, leaving orphaned agents that count against the quota.
Less likely: the per-org quota limit was recently lowered on the swarm backend, causing a previously-passing org to exceed the new threshold.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T22:35:40–44Z with an identical 409 response from POST /api/agents: the swarm backend rejected the creation request because the agent quota for the eval org has reached its hard limit of 100. Because the agent creation call fails immediately, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is ever written, causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend returned HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" on every POST /api/agents call made by the eval runner. The eval org used by the status probes has accumulated 100 swarm agents — the enforced per-org limit — leaving no capacity for the eval to create a new remote agent. Because agent creation is the first step in the runner branch (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339: `const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)`), all downstream evidence collection and contract assertions are skipped, producing a complete evidence gap and a fail status across all three remote-agents checks.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api — Agent Runtime Endpoint Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval targeting the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint was unreachable or not deployed at the URL configured via LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime environment in the same run, isolating the failure to the production-api harness configuration or deployment, not to the image generation logic itself.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api runtime harness endpoint returned a 404 when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream, causing SESSION_OPEN_FAILED before any generation frames could be emitted. Because the session could not be opened, no generation_completed frame was produced and no image URL was returned, causing both contract assertions to fail. The desktop-release sibling check passed in the same run, which rules out a shared upstream dependency failure and localizes the problem to the production-api harness deployment or its URL configuration (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL).
proof: failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message='agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'

failed-check.message: both contract assertions failed — frameTypes expected to contain 'generation_completed' (actual: ['generation_start','generation_error','message']) and imageUrlPresent expected true but got false — as a direct downstream consequence of the 404.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2202, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the stream was aborted at session-open time rather than timing out during generation.

sibling.image-generation-stream: the same check on runtimeEnvironment=desktop-release passed with latencyMs=125667, emitting generation_completed and imageUrlPresent=true, proving the image generation logic and upstream model service are functional.

The production-api harness is running an incompatible version that no longer exposes the /api/generate/image/stream route at the expected path, as stated in the error message.

The access token or authentication context used by the eval runner for production-api is valid (the runner did not skip due to missing token per infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1437) but the harness rejects the session-open request with a 404 due to a routing or version mismatch.
